cohort: The study included 106 neonates born to mothers with early-onset preeclampsia (<34 weeks of gestation) and 106 infants born to normotensive mothers, matched 1-to-1 for sex and gestational age.
finding: Infants born to mothers with early-onset preeclampsia had significantly higher systolic, diastolic, and mean blood pressure values from the second day up to the fourth postnatal week compared with infants born to normotensive mothers.
gest_age: Early-onset preeclampsia was defined as developing at <34 weeks of gestation, and infants were matched 1-to-1 for gestational age.
